newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- prices end slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- prices end slightly higher.

text.p: U.S. Municipal bond prices overcame a stronger-than-expected National Association of Purchasing Management report to end Monday's quiet session modestly higher, market sources said.
"We opened up (higher), and then we lost the bid when purchasing managers came out," one trader said. "Then, little by little, the bid has kind of come back this afternoon as the market recovered."
NAPM's index of manufacturing activity rose to 57.1 in May from 54.2 in April. Economists surveyed by Reuters expected a reading of 53.9.

While traders pegged muni cash as flat at midday, a municipal analyst said dollar bonds ended unchanged to up 1/8 point, mirroring the overall market. High-grade issues ended flat to a basis point better in spots.

Monday's actively quoted issues included Alliance Airport Authority Inc, Texas, special facilities revenue bonds. The 6-3/8 percent bonds due April 2021 were bid at 101-1/2, unchanged from Friday's level.
In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond was up 3/32 at 96-17/32 to yield 6.90 percent in late New York trade.
In debt futures, the September municipal contract closed up 1/32 at 115-16/32. The September T-bond contact closed up 4/32 at 109-24/32. The MOB spread was 184 ticks.
Turning to new issues, Tuesday's municipal bond sales are expected to total $1 billion in 41 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings are expected total $559 million in 20 sales, with a $92.2 million New York State Dormitory Authority deal through Merrill Lynch & Co. topping the list.
On the competitive side, 21 sales totaling $470 million are scheduled. A $200 million New York City deal is the largest.
An additional 10 sales totaling $402 million are on the possible calendar, meaning underwriters have said they may price the issues Tuesday depending on market conditions.
